org chart.d: A diagram that shows the jobs in a company and how they are connected.
org chart.ex: HR gave Luis an org chart on his first week.

reporting line.d: The connection between you and the person you report to.
reporting line.ex: My reporting line goes to the Operations Manager.

chain of command.d: The line of authority from the top of a company to the bottom.
chain of command.ex: Follow the chain of command: talk to your manager first.

direct report.d: A person who reports directly to a specific manager.
direct report.es: subordinado directo, persona a tu cargo

span of control.d: The number of people one manager supervises directly.
span of control.es: tramo de control, número de personas que supervisa un jefe
span of control.ex: Flat companies usually have a wide span of control.

dotted line.d: A second, less formal reporting line, for example to a project leader.
dotted line.ex: I report to Karen, with a dotted line to the project lead.

point of contact.d: The person you should contact about a specific topic.
point of contact.ex: Priya is our point of contact in Finance.

cross-functional.d: Involving people from different departments working together.
cross-functional.ex: The launch needs a cross-functional team.

article.dek: Titles, departments and reporting lines: how to read the map of a U.S. company and find your place in it.
article.title: Who Do I Ask? How U.S. Companies Organize People and Roles

blocks.en: Imagine your first week at a new job. You have one question about your schedule, another about your paycheck, and a third about a project. Who do you ask? In a U.S. company, the answer depends on the structure, and many workers are not sure. In a Gallup survey from late 2024, just under half of U.S. employees strongly agreed that they knew what was expected of them at work, down from 56% in early 2020.{1}
blocks.es: Imagina tu primera semana en un trabajo nuevo. Tienes una duda sobre tu horario, otra sobre tu pago y una tercera sobre un proyecto. ¿A quién le preguntas? En una empresa de EE. UU. la respuesta depende de la estructura, y muchos trabajadores no lo tienen claro. En una encuesta de Gallup de finales de 2024, poco menos de la mitad de los empleados en EE. UU. dijo estar totalmente de acuerdo en que sabía lo que se esperaba de ellos en el trabajo; a principios de 2020 era el 56 %.

blocks.h: The org chart is your map
blocks.en: Most companies show their structure in an [[org chart]]: a diagram where each box is a job and the lines show how the jobs are connected.{2} People are grouped into departments. The most common way is by function, such as Marketing, Finance, Sales or Operations. Companies can also group people by product, by type of customer, or by region, and large companies often mix several of these at once.{2}
blocks.es: La mayoría de las empresas muestran su estructura en un organigrama: un diagrama donde cada caja es un puesto y las líneas muestran cómo se conectan los puestos. Las personas se agrupan en departamentos. La forma más común es por función, como Marketing, Finanzas, Ventas u Operaciones. Las empresas también pueden agrupar a la gente por producto, por tipo de cliente o por región, y las empresas grandes muchas veces combinan varias de estas formas a la vez.

blocks.en: The lines on the chart show the [[chain of command]]: the line of authority from the top of the company to the bottom, which tells everyone who reports to whom.{3} Your [[reporting line]] connects you to your manager, and each person you manage is a [[direct report]]. Traditional companies follow the idea that each employee takes instructions from only one boss. The number of people one manager supervises is called the [[span of control]].{3}
blocks.es: Las líneas del organigrama muestran la cadena de mando: la línea de autoridad desde la parte más alta de la empresa hasta la más baja, que le dice a todos quién le reporta a quién. Tu línea de reporte te conecta con tu jefe, y cada persona que tú supervisas es un subordinado directo. Las empresas tradicionales siguen la idea de que cada empleado recibe instrucciones de un solo jefe. El número de personas que supervisa un jefe se llama tramo de control.

blocks.q_en: Think about your last job. Could you draw your reporting line, from you to the top of the company?
blocks.q_es: Piensa en tu último trabajo. ¿Podrías dibujar tu línea de reporte, desde ti hasta lo más alto de la empresa?

items.en: People with the same skills work together in departments such as Marketing or Finance, and each department has its own manager.{5} You become an expert in your area, but you need to make an extra effort to communicate with other departments.
items.es: Las personas con las mismas habilidades trabajan juntas en departamentos como Marketing o Finanzas, y cada departamento tiene su propio jefe. Te vuelves experto en tu área, pero tienes que hacer un esfuerzo extra para comunicarte con otros departamentos.

items.h: 2 · Divisional: grouped by product or region
items.en: The company is split into divisions, for example by product line or by region, and each division has its own leaders and resources.{5} Each division works almost like a smaller company inside the big one.
items.es: La empresa se divide en divisiones, por ejemplo por línea de producto o por región, y cada división tiene sus propios líderes y recursos. Cada división funciona casi como una empresa más pequeña dentro de la grande.

items.en: People from different functions join project teams, so each person has two supervisors: a functional manager and a project manager.{4} This helps with complex projects, but the double reporting line can create unclear roles and power struggles.{4} People often call the second line a [[dotted line]].
items.es: Personas de distintas áreas se unen a equipos de proyecto, así que cada persona tiene dos supervisores: el jefe de su área y el jefe del proyecto. Esto ayuda en proyectos complejos, pero la doble línea de reporte puede causar roles poco claros y luchas de poder. Muchas veces a la segunda línea se le llama “línea punteada”.

items.en: Flat companies remove many layers of middle management, so employees have more responsibility and more power to make decisions.{5} You may talk directly with senior leaders, but you also need to organize your own work.
items.es: Las empresas planas eliminan muchos niveles de mandos medios, así que los empleados tienen más responsabilidad y más poder para tomar decisiones. Puedes hablar directamente con los líderes de más alto nivel, pero también necesitas organizar tu propio trabajo.

after.subject: Request to change my work hours

body.t: Could I change my hours to 7 AM–3 PM, starting Monday, May 6?
The earlier schedule matches the warehouse shift I support, so I can answer their questions faster.
If there's a form or a process I should follow, I'm happy to complete it. I've sent my benefits question to HR.

marks.en: The right person, and the request comes first with a date.
marks.es: La persona correcta, y la petición va primero con una fecha.

marks.en: A short reason that connects to his role.
marks.es: Una razón corta que se conecta con su rol.

marks.en: He follows the process and sends the other question to its owner.
marks.es: Sigue el proceso y manda la otra duda a quien le corresponde.

blocks.en: You don't need to memorize every box on the chart. You need to know three things: who you report to, who your [[point of contact]] is in other departments, and how to work well in [[cross-functional]] teams. In the case below, you'll follow Luis as he learns this the hard way.
blocks.es: No necesitas memorizar cada caja del organigrama. Necesitas saber tres cosas: a quién le reportas, quién es tu persona de contacto en otros departamentos y cómo trabajar bien en equipos interfuncionales. En el caso que sigue vas a acompañar a Luis mientras lo aprende por las malas.

original.title: Understanding Organizational Structures in the U.S.
original.body_en:
📚 Reading Assignment

Title: Understanding Organizational Structures in the U.S.
Time: ~1 hour

Case Study:
Luis starts a new role at a mid-sized U.S. company. On his first week, he's unsure whether to ask his manager or HR about scheduling questions. After two missteps, he asks HR for help, and they explain the chain of command and give him an organizational chart. Suddenly, things become clearer—he now knows exactly who to report to and who to approach for different issues.

Questions while reading:

What mistakes did Luis make?

How did HR help him better understand the company?

Why is role clarity important for building trust and efficiency?

Article Reference:
🔗 Indeed – Types of Organizational Structures in Business — https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/career-development/types-of-organizational-structures

Video Reference:
🎥 YouTube – Organizational Structures Explained — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FBLzJcP0ic
original.body_es:
📚 Tarea de Lectura

Título: Entendiendo las Estructuras Organizacionales en EE.UU.
Tiempo: ~1 hora

Estudio de Caso:
Luis comienza un nuevo puesto en una empresa estadounidense de tamaño medio. En su primera semana, no está seguro si debe preguntar a su gerente o a Recursos Humanos sobre cuestiones de programación. Después de dos errores, pide ayuda a Recursos Humanos, y ellos le explican la cadena de mando y le dan un organigrama. De repente, las cosas se vuelven más claras: ahora sabe exactamente a quién reportar y a quién acudir para diferentes problemas.

Preguntas mientras lees:

¿Qué errores cometió Luis?

¿Cómo le ayudó Recursos Humanos a entender mejor la empresa?

¿Por qué es importante la claridad de roles para construir confianza y eficiencia?

cases.scene: Luis starts a new role at a mid-sized U.S. company. On Monday, he asks his manager, Karen, how to request time off in the HR system. She tells him that's an HR question. On Tuesday, he emails the Operations Director, Karen's boss, about his work hours:

message.text: Hi Mr. Collins, sorry to bother you. Karen said my time-off question is for HR, so maybe you can help me with my schedule? I'd like to work 7 to 3 instead of 9 to 5, if that's possible.

cases.outcome: The director forwards the email to Karen. Karen is surprised that Luis went over her head.

activity.model:
Hi Karen,
Could I change my hours to 7 AM–3 PM, starting next Monday? It matches the warehouse shift I support. Is there a form or a process I should follow?
Thank you,
Luis
hints_en: Give a date and a short reason
hints_es: Da una fecha y una razón corta
activity.prompt_en: Rewrite Luis's message so it goes to the right person and is clear.
activity.prompt_es: Reescribe el mensaje de Luis para que llegue a la persona correcta y sea claro.

questions: Who should Luis contact first about his work hours? Why?
questions_es: ¿A quién debería contactar Luis primero sobre su horario? ¿Por qué?

cases.scene: After two missteps, Luis asks HR for help. Jasmine from HR replies:

message.text: Hi Luis, happy to help! Here's our org chart so you can see the whole team. For your daily schedule and work hours, talk to Karen first. She's your direct manager. For time off, benefits and pay, contact HR. If you're ever not sure, ask Karen and she'll point you to the right person.

cases.outcome: Luis saves the org chart. Now he knows exactly who to report to and who to approach for different issues.

why.en: It makes clear which topics belong to HR.
why.es: Deja claro qué temas le tocan a Recursos Humanos.

cases.scene: Two weeks later, Luis needs the March sales numbers from Finance for a report.

why.en: Message B is better: Luis writes to the right person, says who he is and where he fits, makes a clear request with a date, and explains why. Message A goes to everyone, has no owner and no deadline, so it wastes people's time.
why.es: El mensaje B es mejor: Luis le escribe a la persona correcta, dice quién es y dónde encaja, hace una petición clara con fecha y explica por qué. El mensaje A va para todos, no tiene responsable ni fecha, así que le hace perder el tiempo a la gente.

options.text: Hi everyone, does anybody know who has the sales numbers? I need them soon. Thanks!

options.lead: Message B, to Priya in Finance:
options.text: Hi Priya, I'm Luis, the new operations analyst on Karen's team. Karen told me you're our [[point of contact]] in Finance. Could you send me the March sales numbers by Thursday? I need them for our monthly delivery report.
